Every button below opens a modal built by the extension as this page was rendered.

This site sets two defaults for all of them, in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
extensions:
  modal:
    fade: true
    centred: true
```

Individual modals below override those.

The dismiss button sits inside the modal it closes, so it uses `inside=true` rather than naming a target.

## The default button type

`type` is the first argument of the shortcode, and it is positional.
Leave it out and you get a toggle button.

{{< modal target=modal-default-type label="Open without a type" >}}

::: {#modal-default-type}

## Opened by a bare toggle

The button that opened this modal named no type at all.

---

{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Close" >}}

:::

````markdown
{{{< modal target=modal-default-type label="Open without a type" >}}}
````

Write the type as a bare word, and never as `type=toggle`.
A named `type` is read as an attribute instead.
The extension then reports a key it does not recognise, and you still get a toggle button.
The [button table](reference.qmd#buttons) lists the two values the argument accepts.

## Dismiss buttons

A dismiss button closes a modal, and it takes more than one shape.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-dismiss label="Open the dismiss example" >}}

::: {#modal-dismiss}

## Three ways to close

Each button in the footer closes this modal.

---

{{< modal dismiss target=modal-dismiss label="Close by name" >}}
{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Cancel" classes="btn btn-secondary" >}}
{{< modal dismiss inside=true >}}

:::

````markdown
{{{< modal dismiss target=modal-dismiss label="Close by name" >}}}
{{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Cancel" classes="btn btn-secondary" >}}}
{{{< modal dismiss inside=true >}}}
````

`target` names the modal to close, so the button works from anywhere in the page.
`inside=true` drops the target, and the button then closes the modal that holds it.
A dismiss button with no label becomes Bootstrap's bare cross, which is the button the header carries.
`classes` replaces the default classes on any button.

## The default width

`size=medium` and `size=default` add no size class at all, so the dialog keeps the width Bootstrap gives it.
Either spelling gives one modal its default width back when a project sets `size` for every modal.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-default-width label="Default width" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-default-width size=medium}

## Medium is the default

`size=medium` is the same width as a modal that sets no size.

---

{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Close" >}}

:::

```markdown
::: {#modal-default-width size=medium}
```

## Static backdrop

`backdrop-static=true` keeps this open when the backdrop is clicked, and `keyboard=false` stops <kbd>Esc</kbd> from closing it.
The close button is the way out.

---

:::

```markdown
::: {#modal-fullscreen fullscreen=lg}
::: {#modal-static backdrop-static=true keyboard=false}
```

`fullscreen=true` fills the screen at every width, and not only below a breakpoint.

## Overriding a project default

This site turns `fade` and `centred` on for every modal.
One container turns either of them off again.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-plain label="No fade, no centring" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-plain fade=false centred=false}

## No fade and no centring

This dialog appears at once, near the top of the window.
Every other modal on this page fades in and sits in the middle.

---

{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Close" >}}

:::

```markdown
::: {#modal-plain fade=false centred=false}
```

An attribute on the container always wins over the project or document setting.

## The header close button

The header carries a close button unless `close-button=false` removes it.
A container with no horizontal rule gets no footer, so the header button is then the only button.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-no-close label="No header cross" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}
{{< modal toggle target=modal-no-footer label="No footer" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-no-close close-button=false}

## No cross in the header

The footer button is the only button here.

---

{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Close" >}}

:::

::: {#modal-no-footer}

## No footer at all

This container holds no horizontal rule, so the extension builds no footer.
The cross in the header closes it.

:::

```markdown
::: {#modal-no-close close-button=false}
::: {#modal-no-footer}
```

Give each modal a header close button or a footer that closes it.
`close-button=false` with no footer leaves a dialog that only the backdrop and <kbd>Esc</kbd> can close.
[Container-only attributes](reference.qmd#container-only-attributes) covers `close-button` and its label.

## Headings inside the body

The first heading becomes the title.
Every later heading stays in the body, and the extension puts the modal identifier in front of its own identifier.
A heading inside a modal can therefore repeat a heading on the page without a clash.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-headings label="Headings in the body" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-headings}

## A code block inside a modal

A code block keeps its copy button inside a modal.
The extension adds a small script whenever it builds a modal.
The script gives each modal its own clipboard handler, with the modal as the container, so the copy works while the dialog holds the focus.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-code label="Code in a modal" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-code}

## Opening a modal from a link

A link whose target is a modal identifier is expanded into a toggle, so a modal can be opened from the middle of a sentence, [like this one](#modal-basic).

```markdown
[like this one](#modal-basic)
```

The explicit Bootstrap attributes work too, when a link would be the wrong element.
A span that carries them opens the modal in the same way, [like this span]{bs-target="#modal-basic" bs-toggle="modal" .btn .btn-link}.

```markdown
[like this span]{bs-target="#modal-basic" bs-toggle="modal" .btn .btn-link}
```

## Accessibility

`description` points at the identifier of an element elsewhere on the page, and becomes the modal's `aria-describedby`.

{{< modal toggle target=modal-described label="Described modal" classes="btn btn-outline-primary" >}}

::: {#modal-described description="described-note" close-button-label="Dismiss this dialog"}

## A described modal

`close-button-label` renames the header's close button for screen readers.

---

{{< modal dismiss inside=true label="Close" >}}

:::

[This paragraph carries the identifier the modal points at.]{#described-note}

```markdown
::: {#modal-described description="described-note" close-button-label="Dismiss this dialog"}
```

The identifier has to exist in the document; the extension warns when it does not, since a dangling `aria-describedby` is worse than none.
